notTheOtherBook: This is SOLIPSICON, not SOLIPSCION with KERA’s rain lesson.

scriptReview.verdict: Pass for book-introduction purpose; retain the approved narration.
scriptReview.opening: Names the novel immediately, explains dual vulnerability within the first three sentences, and distinguishes the fiction’s two perspectives.
scriptReview.continuity: Book-level premise → Kael’s constrained embodiment → Mara’s perceptual uncertainty → specific starting point and reason to follow both accounts.
scriptReview.limits: Some later meta phrasing is broad, but changing it is not necessary for this targeted repair. No new audio requested; preserve measured clips and their text hashes.
scriptReview.protected: Do not depict the military decision/outcome, the operator behind Mara’s experience, Tomas’s later crisis, the roof encounter or its resolution.

sections: source-8 THE MAN WITH TWO FEARS
sourceReview.readScope: Complete current script reread; opening approximately 9,500 characters of each source section rechecked, including source-body description and subsequent material needed to identify protected revelations. Full source extraction and chapter map available; no fresh whole-novel read claimed.
sourceReview.adaptation: Nonhuman geometry is an expressly simplified conceptual projection, consistent with the source’s description of the Loom’s nest displays. Room layout is interpretive; the orange, puzzle, window, lake and opposed rain movement are explicit early source details.

artDirection: Pale mineral green, warm violet, coral and lake blue; quiet flat backgrounds and rich functional foregrounds. Avoid the existing repeated central polygon. Material filaments support nodes, clinic furniture supports people, and all labels belong to objects. Red Hat Display/Text and all three shared film themes remain unchanged.
delivery: First produce unpublished standalone and SHF with shared build --output. Preserve voice. Run all-theme caption/geometry/audio/font checks, add measured opposing-rain movement test, inspect contact sheets, then seek root review before publication.

scenes.composition: An oblique view into a supported dimensional nursery, with the child’s seven connected growth nodes and sensory filaments physically held by a strained membrane; a small human observation opening occupies another depth, not a row of icons. This is a simplified projection, as the novel itself describes its child-facing nest displays.
actions: Show the support membrane holding a distributed living body, without inventing a stable human face or mouth.
A conduit weakens and the seven supported places draw apart slightly; the surrounding structure remains necessary to continued existence.
The observation opening reveals an ordinary human room, making the other viewpoint visible without depicting the later military incident.
Pause the push-pull of the membrane while a human hand hesitates; dependence and imposed experience coexist.
One control trace reaches the observation opening while the child’s own support stays visibly constrained. Do not equate responsibility with freedom from coercion.
Pull the view toward the gap between the two lived positions, preserving the unresolved relation rather than announcing a culprit.
scenes.purpose: Make the opening’s dual vulnerability visible while clearly keeping the story, not a general cosmology lecture, central.
scenes.title: Hunger on both sides
lines: SOLIPSICON places vulnerable children above a world they are pressured to hurt.
Their own continued existence depends on machinery and rewards they cannot escape easily.
The philosophical science fiction also follows human experience from inside that pressure.
Its dual perspective complicates the boundary between a victim and an operator.
A child's dependence can coexist with terrible power over someone else's experience.
The novel makes that contradiction personal before expanding its account of reality.

scenes.composition: A much closer sectional view of the leaking Sphero-Nest and its feeding conduit. Unlike scene one’s relational overview, this scene follows one failed support path from the crack to the living nodes and a utilitarian Loom response surface.
actions: A tiny mist escapes through the actual visible fissure; the source’s opening 31.8 percent appears on the instrument.
Different parts of the distributed body pull toward different supports; the center does not masquerade as a human stomach.
The Loom’s display gives an operational instruction while the supply remains weak; no fabricated score or successful reward is introduced.
A close focus holds the fragile membrane and the body it supports, letting the narration explain vulnerability.
A human-world opening remains small but discernible beyond the instrument; responsibility is not erased by the nursery view.
Finish with the system still supporting and constraining the child, not a monster silhouette or a concluded moral judgment.
scenes.purpose: Ground the unfamiliar embodiment in a concrete failure, replacing the repeated folded polygon and stable cartoon face.
scenes.title: Inside the failing nest
lines: Kael wakes as the support of his dimensional nest begins to fail.
His hunger disperses through a body unlike a human body.
The systems surrounding him translate continued existence into levels and instructions.
That opening establishes vulnerability inside the position that appears to hold power.
The reader must understand his dependence without letting it erase responsibility.
Its unfamiliar embodiment makes that tension harder than an ordinary villain's motive.

scenes.composition: The Belvédère Clinic common room: one large lake-facing window, a seated Mara with an orange and peel, and Tomas at a nearby puzzle table. Exterior rain is blue; its impossible reflection is warm violet on the glass. The glass and view remain a single window, with small ledge labels only if needed for legibility.
actions: Ordinary blue droplets travel downward past the lake view while Mara looks from her orange toward the window.
Violet reflected droplets visibly travel upward from the sill while blue droplets continue down at the same moment; this is actual displacement, not opposite stroke angles.
Mara looks back to the orange peel and then to the reflected movement, keeping the cause unresolved.
Tomas lowers a puzzle piece and looks impatiently toward her; Mara’s orange, the tabletop and the puzzle stay ordinary and stable.
Hold both opposed motions long enough to compare, alongside two people interpreting the same room differently.
Mara remains attentive but uncertain; neither a diagnostic label nor the later operator/roof sequence appears.
scenes.purpose: Make the precise source contradiction perceptible and preserve its mundane, intimate context.

motionContract.outside: Successive short droplet groups move down within the pane, fade at its lower edge and are replaced from the top; reset positions only while invisible.
motionContract.reflection: Successive short groups begin at the sill, move up on the glass, then fade; reset only while invisible.
motionContract.concurrency: Both directions are visible simultaneously during the reflection sentence and again while the narration compares perspectives.
motionContract.measurableCheck: Use muted deterministic seeking within an active batch: outside rain world-space y must increase and reflection world-space y must decrease over the same 400–700 ms interval. Record actual positions and captions, not merely presence of animation tracks.
motionContract.bounds: Rain never travels into the faces, caption-safe area, title or control bar; all groups remain inside the window opening.

scenes.title: A reflection contradicts the window
lines: The human perspective begins with Mara watching rain beside a clinic window.
Its reflection seems to violate what she knows the weather is doing.
She must distinguish an altered perception from a disturbance outside herself.
The novel gives that uncertainty mundane surroundings and another person's impatient response.
Its two perspectives make neither experience a sufficient account of the whole.
The form invites the reader to hold conflicting explanations without dismissing either life.

scenes.composition: Return to the clinic from the seated reading viewpoint, now with the nest shown as the facing conceptual view rather than reusing a centered nest plus tiny rectangle. Mara’s hand and Kael’s supported body remain distinct, both suspended before the next act.
actions: Direct the viewer into the named opening and the clinic scene using a clear change of viewing position.
Retain the physical asymmetry while showing that each viewpoint contains vulnerability.
Let the two situations occupy different scales and materials, avoiding a generic camps/opponents diagram.
Make the human hand’s hesitation visible while the child’s support remains under tension.
Keep the ordinary room and the unfamiliar nest materially legible, so consequences belong to lives rather than merely the architecture.
End on the two unresolved next moves, with the reader invited to follow both accounts; no solution, rescue or outcome is revealed.
scenes.purpose: Preserve the specific starting point and book-level invitation while giving the ending a genuine visual perspective change.
scenes.title: Enter through both vulnerabilities
lines: Begin with Those Who Press Down, then follow the clinic encounter.
Together they establish why power and vulnerability cannot be sorted into separate camps.
This book suits readers drawn to philosophical science fiction and unstable perspectives.
Its central pressure concerns experience imposed by one life upon another.
The strange architecture matters because someone must live inside its consequences.
SOLIPSICON asks you to follow both sides before deciding what their dependence permits.
